cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Could You Just…
cards.instruction: Turn a difficult task into tiny favors until the help quietly becomes most of the task.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've folded that ribbon back on itself, so I've folded mine. Could you hold it against my wedding bouquet?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was making a bow. You need to wrap the stems first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, the wrapping first. Could you wind it round once while you're holding the stems?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Once won't hold them. I'll wrap it down to here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Could you finish with that bow you were showing me? Just tuck the end underneath and pull it tight; I'll hold the scissors.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies a bow fold as initial bouquet wrapping and A3 hides correction by moving to the next small favor; A5 transfers finishing.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 wrap-first correction becomes one-turn request; B4 wider wrapping becomes A5 bow request.

relationship.evidence: B2/B4 contribute credible craft knowledge and voluntary extra wrapping.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 almost-finished grip to add final finishing, completing most of the task through favors.

specificity.evidence: B4 down-to-here leaves an unnecessary visual reference; A5 showing-me invents a demonstration rather than B simply making a bow.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 can ask for that-bow-of-yours without presenting the shared context as a lesson.
